from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of Basis Vectors", [

            "Basis vectors define the transformed space.",
            "Square matrices map space to itself."
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)

        i_hat = Vector(RIGHT, color="#ADD8E6")
        j_hat = Vector(UP, color="#ADD8E6")
        
        i_label = Text("i-hat", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        j_label = Text("j-hat", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(i_hat, 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(j_hat, 'D4')
        
        # Setup static objects
        self.add(i_hat, j_hat)
        self.add(self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'D5'))
        self.add(self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C4'))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        # Show span
        square = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT, RIGHT+UP, UP, color="#D3D3D3", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(square, 'D4', 'D4', scale_factor=2)
        self.add(square)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        self.play(i_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, RIGHT + 0.5*UP),
                  j_hat.animate.put_start_and_end_on(ORIGIN, -0.5*RIGHT + UP))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A 3x2 matrix maps 2D to 3D.", "This embeds 2D space into 3D.", "Imagine a flat plane in 3D."]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Expansion' Scenario: Embedding 2D into 3D", lecture_lines)

        plane_center = plane.get_center()
        i_hat.next_to(plane_center, ORIGIN, buff=0)
        j_hat.next_to(plane_center, ORIGIN, buff=0)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A 2x3 matrix maps 3D to 2D.", "This projects 3D space into 2D.", "Information is lost during projection."]
        self.setup_layout("The 'Projection' Scenario: Compressing 3D into 2D", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        grid_3d = ThreeDAxes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], z_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"color": "#E6E6FA"}).scale(0.5)
        plane_2d = Rectangle(width=3, height=2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(grid_3d.c2p(1, 1, 1))
        
        self.place_at_grid(grid_3d, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(plane_2d, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#E6E6FA"))
        self.play(Create(grid_3d), Write(point))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        self.play(FadeIn(plane_2d))
        projection_line = Line(point.get_center(), plane_2d.get_center(), color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        self.play(Create(projection_line), point.animate.move_to(plane_2d.get_center()))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(FadeOut(projection_line), FadeOut(grid_3d))

outline.topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Basis Vectors
sections.content: Briefly revisit how a matrix represents a coordinate transformation. A square matrix (n x n) maps an n-dimensional space to itself. We establish that columns of a matrix act as the 'new' basis vectors that define the transformed space.
sections.example: Visualizing 2D basis vectors (i-hat, j-hat) as arrows on a graph that stretch or rotate when multiplied by a matrix.

sections.title: The 'Expansion' Scenario: Embedding 2D into 3D
sections.content: Explain a (3x2) matrix. This acts as a transformation from 2D input space (R²) to 3D output space (R³). Geometrically, this represents a 2D plane sitting inside a 3D volume.
sections.example: A 2D flat drawing of a cat being 'lifted' into 3D space by adding a depth coordinate, forming a thin, flat sheet in a 3D room.

sections.title: The 'Projection' Scenario: Compressing 3D into 2D
sections.content: Explain a (2x3) matrix. This acts as a transformation from 3D space (R³) to 2D space (R²). This demonstrates how 3D information is 'squashed' or projected onto a 2D plane.
sections.example: A 3D robotic arm's position being projected onto a 2D security camera sensor, where the depth (Z-axis) is lost to create a flat image.

sections.title: Visualizing the Rank: Why Information is Lost
sections.content: Explain the rank of a matrix as the 'dimensionality' of the output. When transforming dimensions, emphasize that the number of basis vectors determines the geometry: a 3D object flattened into a 1D line if the rank is 1.
sections.example: A 3D wireframe cube being squashed by a (2x3) matrix until it becomes a flat 2D shadow on the floor.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Synthesize the concept: Non-square matrices are essentially 'bridges' between spaces of different dimensions. They either 'embed' lower dimensions into higher ones or 'project' higher dimensions into lower ones.
sections.example: A character in a video game moving from a 3D world (3D coordinates) to a 2D mini-map (2D coordinates) as an application of a (2x3) projection matrix.
